Flyout Menu

A trigger that reveals a floating panel of navigation links — the mega-menu pattern behind PRODUCTS on ironsoftware.com. Built for Top Nav to compose.

3 propsDisclosure, not menuAwaiting Figma

Preview

The visual layer is provisional. This was built ahead of the Figma frame on purpose — the interaction and accessibility contract is the same whatever the panel ends up looking like, and it is the half that is expensive to get wrong. Padding, radius, shadow, panel width and the caret are neutral token placeholders. What should not change is the script or the ARIA.

Still opens on click Still opens on focus Escape still closes
Click a trigger, or tab to it and press Enter. Esc closes and hands focus back. Tabbing past the last link closes it. Pressing anywhere outside closes it. Opening one closes the others — two open panels in a nav is always a bug.

It is a disclosure, not a menu

The obvious-looking role="menu" + role="menuitem" is wrong here, and the live site gets this wrong today. That pattern is for application menus — the Cut/Copy/Paste kind — and it makes two promises this component cannot keep.
  • It strips link semantics. menuitem tells assistive tech the contents are commands, so a screen reader stops announcing “link” and stops offering them in its links list.
  • It commits to arrow-key navigation with a roving tabindex, where Tab leaves the whole menu rather than moving through it. Nobody expects that from a site nav.
  • So this follows the WAI-ARIA APG’s Disclosure Navigation pattern instead: a <button> owning aria-expanded and pointing at the panel with aria-controls, ordinary links inside, and Tab walking them in DOM order. Same as Footer Bar’s Free tools panel.

Measured against ironsoftware.com

The live nav was probed on 2026-08-05 to ground this. Its PRODUCTS panel is DIV.collapse.menuCollapse, toggled display:none → flex on hover. Three things it does that this component deliberately does not:
  • The trigger is an <a href="/suite/">, not a button. Clicking navigates away instead of opening, so the panel is hover-only — unreachable by keyboard and awkward on touch, where the first tap is both the hover and the click.
  • aria-expanded is hard-coded false and never updates, measured while the panel was open. A screen reader is told the thing is closed the entire time it is on screen.
  • aria-haspopup="true" promises a role="menu" that is not there, and there is no aria-controls at all.
The design is the thing worth copying; the markup is not. Here openOnHover adds hover on top of click and focus rather than replacing them, and skips pointerType: 'touch' so a tap is never treated as a hover. It carries a 150ms close delay so a diagonal cursor path from trigger to panel does not drop it.
On a hover flyout a click only ever opens — settled 2026-08-05. The failure that fixes is common and feels broken: the pointer arrives, the panel opens, and the user clicks the trigger anyway because that is what triggers are for, which shuts the panel in their face and leaves it shut until they move away and come back. The rule is narrowed by a :hover test rather than applied blindly, so the keyboard keeps its toggle: a disclosure reporting aria-expanded="true" that refuses to collapse on Enter is a broken contract, and opened by Tab and Enter it still closes on Enter. Try the third trigger above both ways.

Props

PropWhat it does
labelTrigger text. Required.
openOnHoverAdds hover to click and focus. Off by default — hover is only ever an enhancement.
alignstart / center / end — which edge the panel pins to. A wide panel under a trigger near the right of the bar has to hang left or it leaves the viewport.
notchDraws the pointer up at the trigger.
openRender open on first paint — for docs and tests, not for a live nav.
class
The panel is a slot: whatever you put in it becomes the flyout. Its direct children are numbered by the script and rise in turn as it opens, so composing columns needs no hand-numbering — and a column inserted in the middle cannot leave the sequence stale.

Still open

  • No Figma frame yet. Everything visual here is a placeholder. What is needed to reconcile: a node-specific URL, the component set with its variants, and hover/active states drawn — on Footer Bar those were missing from the set and had to be drawn separately afterwards.
  • Where it lives is undecided. This is a standalone component today; it may belong inside Top Nav as a variant instead, which would change whether Top Nav composes it or absorbs it.
